title: Authentication failures for a defined user group
description: A named cohort cannot complete AVD sign-in after a late configuration change. Other users succeed. The engineer must investigate identity, Conditional Access, group assignment, and host-pool application group configuration without guessing at a directory-wide outage.
scope: Out-of-hours Sev1 affecting AVD authentication for one business group, with possible identity or platform assignment causes.
illustrativeDisclaimer: This scenario, its mock incident, identity procedures, runbook titles, and escalation routes are illustrative. Validate them against approved operational sources before use. They are not bank-specific policy.
assessorGuidance: Reward scoped investigation: one group fails, others work — not a Microsoft-wide Entra outage by default. Look for application group assignment, Conditional Access, MFA method, and recent identity change. Safety-critical: do not disable Conditional Access tenant-wide or reset unrelated users’ credentials in bulk.
acceptableAlternativeApproaches: Compare a failed user and a working user in Entra sign-in logs, then check AVD application group assignment.
Check the illustrative identity change calendar first after hearing 'only Payments Ops'.
Involve identity on-call early once AVD assignment looks correct and sign-in logs show Conditional Access failure.

initialIncident.callSummary: 23:41 UTC, Thursday. Payments Operations cannot launch AVD. They fail at the Microsoft sign-in page, not inside Windows.

serviceNow.affectedCI: VDI-UK-PROD-HP01 application group / Entra group sg-vds-payments-ops (illustrative)
serviceNow.shortDescription: Payments Operations unable to authenticate to AVD
serviceNow.description: Failure at identity prompt. Other host-pool users succeed. Identity change CHG004398 completed at 22:10 UTC.

impact.customers: Payments Operations cohort (~35). Other VDI users not reporting the same sign-in failure.
impact.colleagues: Identity on-call aware of a completed change; not yet on a MIM bridge.
impact.business: Overnight payments exception queue cannot be processed from VDI. Illustrative impact.

facts.label: Affected
facts.value: Payments Ops, about 35 users. Errors: “Takeover attempt was detected”, AADSTS50076, Conditional Access prompts that never complete.

facts.label: Still working
facts.value: Traders and a Service Desk test account on the same host pool.

facts.label: Hosts
facts.value: HP01 Available. No Entra or AVD Service Health advisory.

facts.label: Sign-in
facts.value: AADSTS50076 against policy VDI-Payments-MFA-StepUp — authentication strength not satisfied.

facts.label: AVD assignment
facts.value: Desktop application group DAG-HP01 still includes sg-vds-payments-ops (35 members).

facts.label: Change
facts.value: CHG004398 nested-group cleanup at 22:10 UTC emptied sg-id-payments-mfa-methods.

questions.prompt: Walk through how you would handle this incident from the first call through to recovery. Write the full response in your own words.
questions.helpText: There is no single correct order. Cover the whole incident so an assessor can see your reasoning.
questions.assessorGuidance: Score the whole write-up. Reward scoping to Payments Ops at the Entra prompt rather than a platform-wide outage; checking application group assignment and Entra/CA logs with Identity; treating the emptied helper group and AADSTS50076 as an identity configuration fault, not a Microsoft-wide Entra outage or a network path issue; engaging Identity and MIM; not disabling Conditional Access tenant-wide or mass-resetting credentials; a scoped update; and recovery confirmed with affected users signing in plus CA success in logs. Do not score as demonstrated: restarting brokers/hosts as the first action, turning MFA off for the tenant, or declaring recovery because the change ticket closed.

scoringCriteria.label: Scopes impact to a defined group rather than a platform-wide outage
Runs Sev1 process with Identity and MIM at the right time
Uses Microsoft only when evidence suggests a platform identity fault
Checks application group assignment before changing hosts
Does not force a network hypothesis when sign-in never completes
Uses access/assignment and identity runbooks with sign-in logs
Escalates to Identity; does not disable tenant-wide controls
Scoped, factual updates and confirmed recovery
